candidate.name: Joshua Jose
credentials: MSc Data Science, FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg (in progress)

letter.company: Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt e. V. (DLR)
letter.opening: The first task in your posting is the evaluation and validation of machine and deep learning methods against available datasets and benchmarks, and that is the part of this work I have done the most of. The last task is collaboration on scientific publications, where I can point to a peer-reviewed paper rather than a seminar report.
letter.profile_intro: I am an MSc Data Science student at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg, after a BTech in Computer Science and four applied AI and machine learning internships. At Elevate Labs I delivered 10+ production-ready models across regression, classification, forecasting and clustering and was recognised as Best Performer of the cohort. What I would bring to the Galileo Competence Center is less any single model than the habit of settling how a method will be judged before a number is reported.

achievements.lead: Evaluation and benchmarking across the classical stack
achievements.impact: 95%+ ROC-AUC on a Support Vector Machine tuned by GridSearchCV hyperparameter search, 96%+ accuracy on breast-cancer diagnosis and R² above 0.90 on housing-price regression, each judged on the metric that fitted the problem rather than on accuracy by default.
Walmart weekly sales predicted from temporally ordered data at 96.1% R², cutting forecast error by 18%.
Full training, validation and inference pipeline for an American Sign Language recognition model in PyTorch, including data augmentation to improve generalisation.
Co-author of PrisonSecure in the ICISD 2025 proceedings, Atlantis Press (Springer Nature), benchmarked at 95.79% mAP@0.5 with precision and recall both at 0.93 for weapon detection.
200 customers segmented into five clusters with K-Means at a silhouette score of 0.55.

letter.problems_section: Your stated focus on unsupervised and semi-supervised learning for time series is where my experience stops short, and I would rather name that than blur it. My time-series work is supervised, feature-engineered forecasting, and my unsupervised work is K-Means clustering on tabular customer data, so representation learning on telemetry would be new ground. What I can contribute from the first week is the evaluation half of the task list: deciding how a method is judged when labels are scarce is a measurement problem before it is a modelling one.
letter.closing: I am based in Erlangen and can work up to 20 h/week during the semester and full time during official semester breaks. You ask for code examples or a repository: I have no public one to attach. The work sits in internship and coursework repositories and I am glad to walk through any of it.
